option_text: What to test in a machine learning/data science pipeline? › Unit testing feature engineering logic
best_code: Feature-engineering unit tests: The CI process includes unit tests for feature-engineering logic, such as verifying categorical-column one-hot encoding.

option_text: How to integrate a machine learning model in an application? › No integration of the model: model is not integrated, maybe results are used, e.g. as a forecast
best_code: Offline forecast workflow: The Forecast pattern uses an available dataset to train a model and then applies it to mostly historical data to produce predictions, supporting experimentation and educational use.

option_text: How to monitor and track the model in production? › Model performance monitoring: observe specific model performance parameters
best_code: Production performance monitoring: The system tracks model performance on production data and compares predictions with actual outcomes to support model selection and safety assessment.

option_text: What to test in a machine learning/data science pipeline? › Integration testing pipeline components
best_code: Automated end-to-end ML pipeline integration tests: The document recommends regularly triggering the entire ML pipeline and checking that data and code complete every training stage and that the resulting model performs as expected. These tests are required before the model reaches production.

option_text: How to store data used in machine learning applications? › No data store: get data without storing it, e.g. manual ingested raw data or only event streaming
best_code: Event-stream subscription for ML data ingestion: The document presents Kafka, Pulsar, or Segment event streams as an alternative way for ML teams to subscribe to the data they need.

option_text: Which data processing tasks can be performed by a data processing pipeline or component? › Data transformation
best_code: Data integration pipeline: The architecture includes cleansing and transforming source data, with downstream feature enrichment where possible, before it is used by later workflow stages.

option_text: Which tasks can be performed by a model building pipeline or component? › Train multiple model versions with different parameters and/or algorithms
best_code: Multiple model, parameter, and algorithm versions: The production workflow considers maintaining multiple versions of parameters and algorithms to support model iteration and maximize accuracy.

option_text: How to inform clients about prediction result availability? › Polling: clients poll for the results
best_code: Polling-based asynchronous score delivery: As an alternative asynchronous delivery mechanism, scores are stored in a low-read-latency database and the caller periodically polls for available predictions.

option_text: How to serve model predictions or scores? › Precompute serving: precompute models e.g. as forecasts and deliver as reports
best_code: Precomputed model serving: Precompute is identified as one of the serving patterns used to productionize an ML model.

option_text: How to store data used in machine learning applications? › Data service: store data in services
best_code: Microservices architecture for machine learning: The document states that microservices design works best for machine learning because useful algorithms require relevant data, proper scaling, and specialized implementation concerns.

option_text: Should MLOps be used and if so when? › ML Ops

option_text: How to monitor and track the model in production? › Model in-production tracking: track model usage, inputs, outputs, interpretability, and fairness
best_code: Production model monitoring: The document includes model monitoring as an operational practice used to evaluate model performance in production and support timely updates.

best_code: Offline batch model training: The document states that most models are trained offline in batch mode by collecting existing data, applying a learning algorithm, and producing model parameters for later use.

best_code: Model serving deployment mode: The document identifies alternative serving architectures: a REST microservice for online predictions, an embedded model on an edge or mobile device, or a batch prediction system.
